*loosens collar, pours a drink*

Listen to me. You come to me on the day my daughter is to be married... actually, forget that, wrong family. But this code? This code is gonna give me a panic attack worse than that time with the ducks.

## The Hits

### CRITICAL - SQL Injection (Lines 102, 113-115, 137-139, 183-184, 199-200)

```go
query := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = %s", orderID)
```

Madonna! You're concatenating user input directly into SQL. Any wiseguy could drop your entire database. `'; DROP TABLE orders; --` End of story.

**Fix:** Use parameterized queries everywhere. Those who want respect, give respect - to prepared statements.

### CRITICAL - Storing Credit Cards in Plain Text (Line 79, struct line 33)

You're saving credit cards raw in the database AND returning them in responses. PCI compliance? Fuggedaboutit. You're looking at massive fines, lawsuits. This is the kind of thing that gets people whacked... financially.

**Fix:** Never store full card numbers. Use a payment tokenization service.

### CRITICAL - Race Condition in Inventory (Lines 66-72)

You check inventory, THEN reserve it asynchronously with goroutines. What happens when two orders hit simultaneously? Both pass the check, both charge cards, one fails to reserve. You just stole someone's money.

**Fix:** Atomic inventory reservation with proper transactions. No fire-and-forget for money operations.

### HIGH - Missing Error Handling (Lines 45, 57-58, 62-63, many more)

```go
json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&order)  // Ignored error
resp, _ := http.Post(...)               // Payment could fail silently
```

You're ignoring errors on PAYMENT PROCESSING. Customer's card gets declined, you still try to fulfill the order. This is amateur hour.

### HIGH - Variable Capture in Goroutine (Lines 129-135)

```go
go func() {
    // productID and quantity captured by reference
}()
```

Classic loop variable capture bug. All goroutines might use the LAST item's values. You're releasing wrong inventory.

### HIGH - No Authentication/Authorization

Anyone can cancel anyone's order. Anyone can process refunds. Anyone can export ALL credit card data. You need to check if the user OWNS that order.

### MEDIUM - No Transaction Handling (CreateOrder)

Payment charges, inventory reserves, database writes - all separate operations. Any failure leaves the system in an inconsistent state. Use database transactions. All or nothing, like a good heist.

### MEDIUM - Cache Without Mutex (Line 87)

```go
s.cache[strconv.FormatInt(order.ID, 10)] = &order
```

You have a mutex but don't use it consistently. Concurrent map writes = panic.

### LOW - Export Credit Card Data (Lines 199-210)

Even masked, you're dumping card numbers to CSV. Export endpoint needs serious access controls and audit logging.

---

*takes bite of gabagool*

This code "working in staging" means nothing. You know what else worked? My mother's plan to have me whacked. This doesn't go to production until every single one of these gets fixed.

I'm the boss. What I build goes. Until I'm dead. And this code? It dies first.
